pattern: wrapping an imperative helper as a reactive primitive
why: the primitive inevitably re-exposes the imperative helper as a method
instead: widen the helper's args to T|Node<T>; let the caller opt into reactive control

why: ctx can never observe the true absence-of-DATA state
instead: fix the upstream to stop eager-emitting; use prevData[i]===undefined as the never-emitted detector

why: deadlock≠thrash confusion; the process group can't be killed cleanly
instead: one target at a time; bounded -j; kill by process group; direct log + DONE sentinel

why: the design session task table lags the code; opening a 9Q on a stale premise
instead: grep the named symbols + check the landed marker; surface the stale premise as a HALT

pattern: making architectural decisions on your own initiative
why: silently picking a side masks a spec↔code conflict
instead: surface the conflict for the user to call; review multi-file rewrites file by file

pattern: marking active/superseded with prose inside the archive
why: markers rot; active and superseded end up mixed in one directory
instead: split active/archive into physical directories; put the state in a jsonl status field

pattern: canonical responsibility split across multiple documents
why: the sequencer/decision-log is scattered in many places, causing migration-period confusion
instead: a single canonical per responsibility; decisions in a single D# sequence
